articles.title: As blockchain investing falls out of vogue, a16z Crypto rebrands as a16z Frontier
articles.full_text:
In a sign that crypto and blockchain-focused investing has receded in importance, Andreessen Horowitz announced Thursday that it is renaming its digital asset unit from a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier.

The practice, helmed by Chris Dixon, has raised nearly $10 billion across five funds since launching in 2018, backing some of the sector’s biggest wins, including Coinbase. Yet for years, a16z and rival venture firms struggled to push crypto’s utility beyond financial rails, trading applications, and speculative assets.

Under the new name, the team is broadening its mandate to focus on emerging technologies, be it AI, robotics, or “new kinds of networks” connecting humans and machines. Yet, the group isn’t abandoning crypto. Dixon wrote in a blog post that blockchain technology could “give new networks native economic capabilities.”

Alongside Dixon, a16z Frontier’s general partners include Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet. Meanwhile, Ali Yahya, who joined the crypto strategy as its first investor in 2017, has left the firm, according to The Information.
articles.summary:
Andreessen Horowitz is rebranding its digital asset practice from a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier, signaling a broader strategic shift amid a cooling crypto investment climate. The move keeps blockchain in the mix while expanding the team's focus to AI, robotics, and new human-machine networks.

  • Core event: The venture firm announced Thursday that its crypto unit, led by Chris Dixon, will now operate as a16z Frontier, widening its mandate beyond digital assets to emerging technologies such as AI and robotics.
  • Background: Since launching in 2018, the practice has raised nearly $10 billion across five funds and backed major sector wins including Coinbase, though it has long struggled to push crypto's utility beyond financial rails and speculative assets.
  • Leadership changes: a16z Frontier's general partners include Dixon, Eddy Lazzarin, and Guy Wuollet, while Ali Yahya, the crypto strategy's first investor in 2017, has departed the firm.
  • Impact: The rebrand reflects crypto's receding priority for the storied VC firm, though Dixon said blockchain could still "give new networks native economic capabilities," suggesting crypto remains part of the frontier thesis.
